title: Business Central 2026 release wave 1 (BC28): Experience improved usability in manufacturing
summary: BC28 (2026 wave 1) improves manufacturing usability by enhancing serial-tracked item handling in output journals, ensuring capacity and overhead costs post to location-specific WIP accounts, and adding customizable notifications for non-certified BOMs and routings.
key_points: Explode Routing in the Output Journal now follows item tracking, so serial-tracked items get one line with quantity 1 per serial number while lot-tracked items stay on a single line
Value entries linked to capacity ledger entries now carry the location code from the production order line or item journal line
Capacity and overhead postings use the Inventory Posting Setup for the production location, which keeps WIP accounts balanced
You no longer need an Inventory Posting Setup line for a blank location just to post overhead
A new My Notifications setting lets each user turn warnings about non-certified production BOMs and routings on or off

quotes.text: For serial-tracked items, Business Central splits the last routing operation into multiple lines with quantity 1 per serial number.
quotes.why_it_matters: This ensures accurate production output recording for tracked items without manual workarounds.

quotes.text: Business Central uses the production location when posting capacity and overhead.
quotes.why_it_matters: This prevents WIP account imbalances when material and costs are posted to different locations.

quotes.text: Now, Microsoft has added a new My Notifications setting so you can control whether to display warnings for non-certified production BOMs and routings.
quotes.why_it_matters: Users can reduce notification noise while maintaining oversight of non-certified structures.
